doing some testing, I can recreate the error, printing the dimensions at the time of the error I'm getting it's generating an 8192x65536 pixel Image, which is 536,870,912 total pixels, the max pixel limit is half that at 268,435,456. 

the error message is a bit misleading still as it prints the max size as 16777216x16777216 which is  281,474,976,710,656, and not max pixel value and it might want to be printed as 16384x16384 instead, which appears to be the max texture size

The limit is because higher dimensions can't be handled correctly I guess. But the issue is that directional lightmaps causes this while regular don't. I wonder if this PR could potentially fix this issue https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100790

@BlueCube3310

tried that branch to see, it helps but not enough for directional at 10 texel scale  brings it down to 402,653,184 total pixels, unsure if undirectional is better, both main and that branch dont bake for me at 20 like you were able to crashes without output

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6b7d906-d059-440b-bde6-361abba81c30)

LightmapGI has a system in place for situations like this, it's supposed to split the lightmaps into multiple textures. The issue is that it only functions in situations when the atlas' height exceeds 16777216, which happens less often than simply going over the maximal pixel count

I can confirm this on 4.8.dev 00462d686 (Linux).
